title: Filter-sterilize and QC a supplemented medium
summary: Prepare a synthetic 500 mL serum- and glutamine-supplemented medium, verify stock arithmetic and physicochemical QC, filter through 0.22 µm, document integrity and sterility evidence, and store a traceable quarantined batch.
scenario: Two serum lots, two glutamine aliquots and two receiving bottles are available. One serum lot is expired, one glutamine aliquot has a room-temperature history, and one receiving bottle is unlabelled; inspect the records to identify which. A component lot may also carry an invisible mollicute contamination or a visibly culturable contaminant. Prepare a generic 500 mL batch and preserve its QC and lot trail. All materials and outcomes are synthetic.
guided_steps: Inspect all component, supplement, filter and receiving-bottle records before adding anything; reject the expired serum lot, room-temperature glutamine aliquot and unlabelled receiver.
Add 50 mL from the in-date, undiluted serum lot for a 10% final fraction.
Add 5 mL from the cold-history 100× glutamine aliquot (200 mM stock to 2 mM final); basal medium makes the final total 500 mL, so its volume is 445 mL.
Mix and measure pH and osmolality with a calibrated pH meter and osmometer; the synthetic windows are pH 7.10–7.30 and 280–310 mOsm/kg.
Select the 0.22 µm PVDF filter for the protein-containing medium.
Prime/pre-rinse according to the device procedure, assemble aseptically, and collect in the labelled sterile receiving bottle.
Perform and record a supported bubble-point or pressure-hold integrity test; visual clarity alone is not an integrity test.
Reserve the 10 mL QC control first: with 490 mL recovered from the 500 mL batch, aliquot count × volume per aliquot must not exceed 480 mL.

Label the formulation, dedicated cell line, preparation date 2026-11-15 and synthetic expiry 2026-11-29; copy the exact original synthetic basal, selected serum, selected glutamine and filter lot IDs from the supply/filter evidence.
Draw a 10 mL representative filtrate sterility control with a fresh sterile pipette.
Incubate at least 7 days at 20–25 °C followed by at least 7 days at 30–35 °C; practise lesson 1’s schedule rather than interpreting early clarity.
Submit a dedicated mycoplasma lot test because 0.22 µm filtration does not assure mollicute removal.
Store at 2–8 °C protected from light and quarantine until required QC is acceptable.
Finish to review the calculated batch result, hidden lots, QC outcomes and 14-checkpoint debrief.

checkpoints.description: Inspect all component, supplement, filter and receiving-bottle records before preparation.
checkpoints.rationale: Early inspection identifies expired, poorly stored or unidentified materials before they enter the batch.
An expired supplement has an unknown handling and suitability history and is not rescued by clarity.

source.note: Synthetic label decision; actual expiry comes from the product label.

checkpoints.description: Use the glutamine aliquot with a documented frozen/cold history.
checkpoints.rationale: Glutamine degradation depends on storage history; repeated warming and thawing can change the supplement.

checkpoints.description: Use 50 mL serum and 5 mL 100× glutamine for a 500 mL final batch.
checkpoints.rationale: The stock calculations use final volume, and basal medium is the remaining 445 mL.

source.note: C1V1 = C2V2; exact synthetic values.

checkpoints.description: Measure pH 7.10–7.30 and osmolality 280–310 mOsm/kg with appropriate methods.
checkpoints.rationale: Colour cannot replace pH or osmolality measurement; both evaluate different preparation properties.

source.note: Synthetic QC window and instrument model, not universal acceptance criteria.

checkpoints.description: Use an aseptically assembled, primed 0.22 µm PVDF filter.
checkpoints.rationale: Heat-labile supplemented medium is filtered; membrane compatibility, assembly and priming matter in addition to nominal pore size.

checkpoints.description: Record a supported bubble-point or pressure-hold integrity result.
checkpoints.rationale: A nominal pore-size label and visual clarity do not demonstrate membrane integrity or exclude bypass.

source.note: Simplified integrity-test model; use the actual filter device instructions.

checkpoints.description: Collect filtrate in the receiving bottle with a complete pre-existing identity label.
checkpoints.rationale: An unlabelled receiver has unknown history and cannot be made traceable retrospectively.

checkpoints.description: Draw a 10 mL filtrate control with a fresh pipette and incubate for at least 14 valid days.
checkpoints.rationale: A representative sample and sufficient incubation are required before no visible growth can be interpreted.

checkpoints.description: Incubate at least 7 days at 20–25 °C followed by at least 7 days at 30–35 °C.
checkpoints.rationale: The teaching schedule starts at the lower temperature and then supports recovery at the higher temperature.

checkpoints.description: Submit a dedicated mycoplasma test for the filtered batch.
checkpoints.rationale: Mollicutes can pass 0.22 µm filters and remain invisible to ordinary turbidity checks.

checkpoints.description: Record formulation, dedicated cell line, preparation/expiry dates and the exact basal, selected serum, selected glutamine and filter lot IDs from supply/filter evidence.
checkpoints.rationale: Exact linked lot identifiers support traceability and later investigation; a lot-linkage attestation without those IDs is insufficient.

checkpoints.description: Store the supplemented medium at 2–8 °C protected from light.
checkpoints.rationale: Cold, dark storage limits degradation while product-specific storage instructions remain controlling.

checkpoints.description: Keep the batch quarantined until required QC evidence is acceptable.
checkpoints.rationale: Immediate clarity and filtration are insufficient release evidence for this teaching workflow.

source.note: Simplified quarantine decision, not a validated product-release specification.

limitations: All formulations, lots, readings, containers, labels and events are synthetic; the model does not validate a physical preparation, filter or product.

The 500 mL recipe, pH 7.10–7.30 and 280–310 mOsm/kg windows, volume-weighted osmolality approximation, 98% recovery, 10 mL control, 14-day expiry and hidden-event probabilities are simulation choices, not laboratory acceptance criteria.
The volume-weighted osmolality calculation is an accounting approximation, not a thermodynamic mixing model; measured complete-medium QC and product-specific limits govern real work.

The integrity, sterility and mycoplasma assays are simplified deterministic outcomes and do not model device-specific integrity limits, specimen quality, assay sensitivity, false results or viral clearance.
FDA CGMP process-simulation incubation is adapted for teaching and does not establish regulatory compliance or a validated compendial sterility test.
Aseptic hand technique, cabinet operation and waste handling are practised in lesson 1; this model assesses connected decisions and records, not psychomotor skill or laboratory competency.
